in_sanskrit.name: राजर्षि
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who rules over the sages

in_hindi.name: राजर्षि
in_hindi.long_meaning: राजा (Rājā) - King, ऋषि (Riṣi) - Sage. The name 'Rajarshi' translates to 'King of Sages' or 'Ruler of Seers' in Sanskrit.

in_tamil.name: ராஜர்ஷி
in_tamil.long_meaning: ஆதரவுவன் (Arasan) - Seer, அரசர் (Arasar) - Ruler. The name 'Rajarshi' translates to 'Seer-Ruler' or 'Seer-King' in Tamil.

in_telugu.name: రాజర్షి
in_telugu.long_meaning: రాజ్యశ్శ (Rājyaśśa) - King, శేఖరదేశ (Śēkharadēśa) - Lord of the senses. The name 'Rajarshi' translates to 'Lord of the senses, King' or 'King of the senses' in Telugu.

in_marathi.name: Rajarshi
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Ruler of Kings
in_marathi.long_meaning: Rajarshi हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। One who rules over kings or a wise king

in_bengali.name: Rajarshi
in_bengali.meaning: হিন্দু নাম যার অর্থ Ruler of Kings
in_bengali.long_meaning: Rajarshi একটি হিন্দু নাম যা ভারতীয় সংস্কৃতিতে গভীর আধ্যাত্মিক তাৎপর্য রাখে। One who rules over kings or a wise king

data.cultural_impact: The name "Rajarshi" is a compound of two Sanskrit words - "Raja" meaning king and "Rishi" meaning a wise person. This title has been used historically to denote a wise and just ruler, one who rules with wisdom and knowledge, thereby embodying the qualities of a true leader. In Hindu society, the title has been bestowed upon respected monarchs and spiritual leaders alike, symbolizing the union of power and wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Rajarshi" carries significant spiritual weight for Hindus as it represents a leader who has transcended material desires and emotions, and has attained a state of enlightenment. It signifies a deep understanding of the world, a righteous rule, and a strong spiritual connection to the universe. The name evokes a sense of reverence for the bearer's inner wisdom, courage, and purity. The title serves as a reminder that true power comes from within and that wisdom is the foundation of a just and fulfilling rule, both in the material and spiritual realms.

historical_references.reference: Rajarshi Bhoj I, the powerful Paramara King of Malwa (Central India), known for his great patronage of art and learning.
